english.title: Conspire to sexually assault a female aged 13 or over - no penetration
english.standardoffencewording:
On **(..SPECIFY DATE..) at **(..SPECIFY TOWNSHIP..) conspired together with

(A)_[**(..SPECIFY THE PERSON..)]_
(B)_[**(..SPECIFY THE PERSONS..)]_
(C)_[another person]_
(D)_[other persons]_

to intentionally touch a

(E)_[girl aged13]_
(F)_[girl aged14]_
(G)_[girl aged15]_
(H)_[woman aged 16 or over]_

and that touching would have been sexual when she did not consent and you did not reasonably believe that she would have consented
english.legislation: Contrary to section 1(1) of the Criminal Law Act 1977.

investigatoraction.description: Attracts liability for entry on sex offenders register
Consider an application for a sexual harm prevention order after conviction

DNA Samples: If crime scene stain present - take evidential sample If no crime scene stain and DNA not confirmed on PNC - take Criminal Justice sample. If DNA confirmed on PNC - CJ sample not required
Confirm proposed charge is appropriately authorised (Police or CPS)
Ensure compliance with investigator's obligations re disclosure
Consider if case suitable for referral to Financial Investigation Unit and CPS for asset recovery eg confiscation order

english.notes:
(i) See section 72 of, and Schedule 2 to, the Sexual Offences Act 2003 regarding the committing of this offence outside the UK by UK nationals / residents.
(ii) A person guilty of this offence is subject to notification and orders as provided by section 80 of the Act. (Sch 3 paragraph 19).
(iii) Whether a belief is reasonable is to be determined having regard to all the circumstances, including any steps the offender has taken to ascertain whether the victim consented - (section 3(2)).
(iv) Victim's age should be proved by reference to a Birth Certificate where possible.
(v) The Court of Appeal case R v H (The Times 08/02/05) held that (that in those particular circumstances) a defendant who grabbed at the tracksuit bottoms worn by a female complainant had touched another person for the purpose of a sexual assault.
(vi) Where this offence is committed against an emergency worker this must be treated as an aggravating factor in sentencing, see section 67 of the Sentencing Act 2020.
